newsitem.title: USA: Texas' corn crop completely harvested.
newsitem.headline: Texas' corn crop completely harvested.

text.p: Texas producers wrapped up their corn harvest during the week ended Sunday, the weekly state crop report said.
The report said a midweek cold front brought much cooler temperatures and scattered rainfall to many areas.
Rainfall was minimal in the High Plains, allowing harvesting to proceed without much delay, but a hard freeze did occur as the front passed through northern areas.
Growth of small grains continued to be good across the Plains, but a good rain would help. Harvest of sorghum made good progress, but many fields still remain too green.
Wheat planted 99 percent vs 98 week ago, 87 year ago, 89 on a five-year average.
Wheat emerged 94 percent vs 92 w/a, 71 y/a, 74 avg.
Wheat rated 69 percent of normal, vs 76 w/a, 61 y/a.
Corn harvested 100 percent vs 98 w/a, 99 y/a, 100 avg.
Sorghum harvested 89 percent vs 83 w/a, 95 y/a, 93 avg.
Cotton bolls opening 97 percent vs 95 w/a, 92 y/a, 93 avg.
Cotton harvested 47 percent vs 41 w/a, 53 y/a, 53 avg.
Cotton rated 65 percent good/excellent vs 69 w/a, 62 y/a.
Pasture and range condition was rated 34 percent good to excellent, versus 38 percent at that level last week.
